items.statement: The agreement's official title is 'Agreement on Cooperation in the Field of Security between the Republic of Bulgaria and Ukraine'. The signed text is dated Kyiv, 30 March 2026, and names caretaker Prime Minister Andrey Gyurov and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky as the signatories.
items.quote: СПОРАЗУМЕНИЕ ЗА СЪТРУДНИЧЕСТВО В ОБЛАСТТА НА СИГУРНОСТТА МЕЖДУ РЕПУБЛИКА БЪЛГАРИЯ И УКРАЙНА ... Подписано в Киев на 30 март 2026 г. в два екземпляра на български, украински и английски език, като всички текстове са еднакво автентични.
items.source: Council of Ministers of Bulgaria, full text of the agreement (PDF)

items.statement: The premise that Gyurov signed a framework agreement in Kyiv in 2022 is not supported: the signed text and all contemporaneous reporting place the signing on 30 March 2026. The only 2022 instrument the agreement cites is a defence-ministry agreement on gratuitous transfers of weapons, equipment and ammunition, signed in Sofia on 5 December 2022 - not in Kyiv and not by Gyurov. No 2022 Kyiv agreement signed by Gyurov was found in the official record.
items.quote: Споразумението между Министерството на отбраната на Република България и Министерството на отбраната на Украйна относно безвъзмездно предоставяне на въоръжение, техника и боеприпаси, подписано в София на 5 декември 2022 г.
items.source: Council of Ministers of Bulgaria, full text of the agreement (PDF)

items.statement: The text expressly places itself outside the 1969 Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties and says it sets out 'political commitments'; it enters into force on signature and runs for ten years. The Council of Ministers' own explainer says it contains no legally binding obligations and that implementation depends on national law and parliamentary decisions. The word 'framework' does not appear in the signed text; that is Gyurov's label.
items.quote: Това споразумение не попада в обхвата на Виенската конвенция за правото на договорите (1969 г.) и предвижда политически ангажименти. | Той не попада в приложното поле на Закона за международните договори на Република България, като не съдържа правнообвързващи ангажименти, а възможности за допълнително развитие на съвместни отбранителни способности.
items.source: Council of Ministers of Bulgaria, agreement text and official explainer of 31.03.2026

items.statement: The agreement contains no clause requiring ratification of every contract concluded under it. It only provides that authorised institutions of the parties 'may conclude implementing and technical agreements' in specific areas; nothing in the text makes each such agreement subject to parliamentary ratification. Gyurov asserted in the debate that 'every one of these contracts is subject to ratification by the National Assembly', but that is his interpretation, not a provision of the signed text; whether a future implementing agreement needs ratification would depend on its content and Bulgarian law.
items.quote: Упълномощените институции на всеки от участниците могат да сключват изпълнителни и технически споразумения по конкретни области на сътрудничество в рамките на изпълнението на настоящото споразумение.
items.source: Council of Ministers of Bulgaria, full text of the agreement (PDF)

items.statement: On Belene, the text speaks only of a 'potential sale' of equipment acquired for the Belene nuclear project to Ukraine and of steps to finalise the process; it does not transfer or hand over the reactors. Gyurov said at the signing that the decision rests with the Bulgarian parliament, and the BTA report of the same day repeats that the parliamentary decision is required.
items.quote: Участниците ще продължат да работят по потенциалната продажба на оборудване, придобито за проекта АЕЦ „Белене“, на Украйна, и ще предприемат необходимите стъпки за финализиране на процеса.
items.source: Council of Ministers of Bulgaria, full text of the agreement (PDF); BTA, 30.03.2026

items.statement: On drones, the text does not commit Bulgaria to joint drone production. It lists UAVs among Ukrainian battlefield technologies whose transfer, innovation and joint experimental testing are to be encouraged, and it provides for joint production of 'priority weapons and ammunition' and industrial lines for ammunition. At the Kyiv press conference Zelensky nevertheless said the agreement covered joint production of various weapons 'including drones' - a political statement, not an operative clause of the text.
items.quote: Участниците отчитат стратегическата важност на технологиите, разработени и използвани на бойното поле от Украйна, включително безпилотни летателни апарати ... и подчертават взаимните ползи от трансфера на технологии, иновации и съвместните експериментални тестове на системи и продукти от споделен интерес.
items.source: Council of Ministers of Bulgaria, full text of the agreement (PDF); Ukrinform, 30.03.2026

items.statement: The agreement does mention the 'Coalition of the Willing': the parties say they value its work and confirm their engagement with its activities. It does not create formal membership or an automatic commitment to deploy troops; it is a political affirmation, and the text elsewhere says implementation must follow national law and parliamentary decisions.
items.quote: Участниците оценяват високо важната работа на Коалицията на желаещите и потвърждават своята ангажиментност към нейните дейности.
items.source: Council of Ministers of Bulgaria, full text of the agreement (PDF)

items.statement: A full-text search of the 20-page signed agreement finds no mention of Bulgarian soldiers or Bulgarian military personnel being sent to Ukraine. The only military-personnel references concern Ukrainian service members (English-language training, Ukrainian officers on Bulgarian naval vessels), and the implementation section requires compliance with national law and parliamentary decisions. The ZaKogo/Focus fact-check reached the same conclusion: the document does not provide for sending Bulgarian troops to Ukrainian territory.
items.quote: България ще продължи да осигурява обучение по английски език за украински военнослужещи, по искане на Украйна, както и обучение на английски език за украински пилоти и техници.
items.source: Council of Ministers of Bulgaria, full text of the agreement (PDF); Focus/ZaKogo fact-check, 30.10.2026

items.statement: In the 29 October 2026 BNT debate, Ilyana Yotova asserted that Gyurov signed the ten-year agreement without a National Assembly mandate, 20 days before the election, and that it contains commitments to hand over the Belene reactors, produce drones and join the 'Coalition of the Willing'. She also said the document was written two years before the Kyiv trip.
items.quote: Без мандат на Народното събрание и без да ми кажете 20 дни преди изборите подписахте документ, с който накарахте държавата за 10 години да поеме ангажименти. ... Това не е отворена врата, а поети ангажименти да предадем реакторите от „Белене“, да произвеждаме дронове ... да сме в коалицията на желаещите.
items.source: 24 Chasa (168 Chasa), report/transcript of the BNT debate

items.statement: Gyurov replied that the document had been in the National Assembly and that 'the speaker returned it, saying the power to sign lies with the government'; he called it a 'framework agreement' under which Bulgarian companies could take part in Ukraine's reconstruction but no Bulgarian soldiers would be sent.
items.quote: За споразумението с Украйна - то беше в Народното събрание. Председателят го върна и каза, че правомощието за подпис е на правителството. ... Това е рамково споразумение ... но не и да се пращат български войници в Украйна.
items.source: 24 Chasa (168 Chasa), report/transcript of the BNT debate

items.statement: On 18 December 2024 caretaker Prime Minister Dimitar Glavchev formally asked the National Assembly, through Speaker Natalia Kiselova, for a specific mandate to sign the ten-year security agreement, citing its long-term framework and the Constitutional Court's case law on caretaker governments. This shows that no mandate existed at that point; the request was never put to a vote.
items.quote: С оглед предвидената дългосрочна рамка (10-годишен срок на действие) в духа на парламентарното управление, в изпълнение на Конституцията и практиката на Конституционния съд призовавам Народното събрание да даде нарочен мандат на служебното правителство за подписване на Споразумението за сътрудничество в областта на сигурността между Република България и Украйна.
items.source: Council of Ministers of Bulgaria, press release of 18.12.2024

items.statement: Speaker Natalia Kiselova refused to table the mandate request: on 19 December 2024 she said she would not put the draft agreement to a vote because it fell within the government's competence and the government had already authorised the Prime Minister to sign it. She later wrote that the 51st National Assembly 'did not give a mandate' and that she did not submit the approval request. No National Assembly mandate was ever voted; Gyurov signed on 30 March 2026 without one, and in 2026 Kiselova said the National Assembly had not been informed. No formal text of a speaker's letter 'returning' the document was located; Gyurov's account that the speaker returned it is his characterization of this refusal.
items.quote: Няма да внеса проекта на Споразумение с Украйна за сътрудничество в областта на сигурността за гласуване в пленарната зала. ... Тъй като има нарочно изрично решение на правителството, министър-председателят трябва да се съобрази с него, а не да търси подкрепа и да прехвърля отговорността на Народното събрание.
items.source: BNR Horizont, 19.12.2024; Natalia Kiselova Facebook post, 31.03.2026 (reproduced by 5GMedia)

open_questions: No verbatim text of a formal speaker's letter 'returning' the agreement or the mandate request to the government was located. The documented action is Speaker Natalia Kiselova's refusal on 19 December 2024 to table the request, with the reasoning that signing fell within the government's competence; Gyurov later described this as the speaker 'returning' the document. Whether a formal letter exists and its exact wording remain unconfirmed.

The '2022' premise is not supported: no 2022 Kyiv agreement signed by Andrey Gyurov was found. The only 2022 instrument cited in the signed text is the defence-ministry agreement signed in Sofia on 5 December 2022. In the debate Yotova said the document was 'written two years before' the Kyiv trip (i.e. 2024), not 2022; the origin of the 2022 date could not be pinned to a verbatim statement.

Whether any implementing or technical agreements under the framework have already been signed, and whether any of them required ratification, is not established; the text contains no ratification clause and no such contracts were located.

The agreement's legal effect is contested: Sofia calls it a non-binding political act outside the Vienna Convention, while Kyiv's Presidential Office described it as fixing 'clear obligations' for Bulgaria. No court ruling or authoritative legal opinion on its status was found.
Whether the Ukrainian Verkhovna Rada ratified the agreement (as distinct from the Bulgarian National Assembly) was not established; no such ratification act was found.
Some pages could not be used: OFFNews and Dnevnik returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare), and the BTA debate article's body could not be extracted from its page; those pages were not relied on.
notes: The cluster is strong on the document itself: the full 20-page signed text was obtained from the Council of Ministers (gov.bg) and is also preserved in the Wayback Machine, so the title, Kyiv date of 30 March 2026, ten-year term, 'political commitments' / Vienna Convention exclusion, Belene 'potential sale' wording, UAV/technology wording, the single 'Coalition of the Willing' sentence and the complete absence of any Bulgarian-troop deployment clause are documented primary facts. It is also solid on the mandate chronology: Glavchev's 18 December 2024 written request for a mandate, Kiselova's 19 December 2024 refusal to table it, and her later statement that the 51st National Assembly gave no mandate. The weaker points are (a) the '2022' premise, which the record contradicts and appears to conflate the 5 December 2022 Sofia defence-ministry agreement or the 2024 draft with the 2026 signing; (b) the 'speaker's letter', for which only Kiselova's public refusal and Gyurov's retrospective account exist, not the letter itself; and (c) the bindingness question, where Sofia's 'political commitments' reading and Kyiv's 'clear obligations' reading diverge. The drone-production claim is supported by Zelensky's press statement but not by an explicit obligation in the text, and Gyurov's 'framework' and 'every contract needs ratification' formulations are his characterizations rather than terms of the signed document. A further characterization gap: Kyiv's Presidential Office described the agreement as fixing 'clear obligations' for Bulgaria (Ukrainska Pravda/Yevropeiska Pravda, 31.03.2026, https://www.eurointegration.com.ua/_barcelona/news/2026/03/31/7234397/), while Sofia calls it non-binding - the same document is being sold differently in the two capitals.
